title: Graph valid tree
label: idb-list
statement: You have `n` nodes numbered 0 to n−1 and a list of undirected edges. Say whether these edges make the nodes into **one valid tree**: everything connected, and no cycles.
provenance: **InterviewDB-listed.** LeetCode 261 is on the LinkedIn list you supplied from InterviewDB. No candidate report of this exact question was found in the research passes — the evidence is that the list names it. On that list it uses the same pattern as InterviewDB Q2, Q15. Cycle detection plus connectivity. Q2 needs the *undirected* walk over every component; Q15 needs the *directed* one, where a cycle means a back edge to a node still on the current path. 261 is the cleanest place to get the undirected version right.

1.q: Why is the edge count enough with union-find?
1.a: n − 1 edges and no cycle means n − (n − 1) = 1 component.

2.a: Also fine: count edges, then check one BFS reaches all n nodes.

3.a: Union-find under one lock is simple; lock-free union-find exists but is rarely worth it.

4.a: Distributed connected components (label propagation) — far harder; say so.

5.a: InterviewDB Q15 (task dependencies) is the directed version: cycle detection by topological sort.

prompts.label: Check my design — no code
prompts.text: I believe a tree has exactly n − 1 edges; with that count, union-find finding no edge inside one group proves it connected and acyclic — O(n · α(n)). Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?

prompts.label: Tests that expose bugs

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: You have `n` nodes numbered 0 to n−1 and a list of undirected edges. Say whether these edges make the nodes into **one valid tree**: everything connected, and no cycles.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Can an edge repeat, or connect a node to itself? (Treat either as a cycle.)
- Is n = 1 with no edges a tree? (Yes.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: A tree on n nodes has exactly n − 1 edges. With exactly that many, "no cycle" and "connected" are the same condition — so check the count, then use union-find: an edge whose two ends are already connected closes a cycle.

learn.title: 4 · Approach

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Checking only for cycles and forgetting connectivity (or the reverse).
- A DFS that treats the parent edge as a cycle in an undirected graph.
- Recursive DFS overflowing on a long chain.
